findings.title: factor_relative in evaluate() compares a full symmetric prediction against a triangle-only label; a perfect prediction reports ~0.28, not 0
findings.claim: `train_equi.unpack` (line 59-66) only writes `out[row, row:]`, so it returns the STRICTLY UPPER triangle of the packed label with zeros below the diagonal. That is correct for `R_UPPER.npy` (genuinely upper triangular) but wrong for `MQ_UPPER.npy`, which is the packed upper triangle of a SYMMETRIC q x q matrix. Line 221 loads the M_q label this way and line 222 subtracts it from `M`, which `predict_full_q` has just asserted to be exactly symmetric (line 198). The reported `factor_relative` therefore carries the entire strict lower triangle of the label as fake error. The same file symmetrises correctly 49 lines later (line 270: `M0 = M0 + torch.triu(M0, 1).T`) and so does `platen.py:37`, so the omission at line 221 is an oversight, not a convention.
findings.failure_scenario: Feed the exact label back as the prediction for seat 0253 (q=12828). The true factor_relative is 0. What SPECTRUM.json reports is ||tril(M,-1)||_F / ||triu(M)||_F = sqrt((F^2-D^2)/(F^2+D^2)) with F = ||M_q||_F = 27277.44 and D = ||diag(M_q)||_2. Using the builder's own logged pivot statistics (log_pivot_mean 3.4603, log_pivot_std 1.3942, n=12828) D ~= 2.52e4, giving ~0.283. The three A1 arms will each write factor_relative >= ~0.28 into EVAL_0253/SPECTRUM.json and RESULT.json['evaluations'], which handover section 2.1 says to download to docs/data/equi_20260918/A1_<arm>_*.json and compare. A reader concludes 'the network is 28-40 % off in Frobenius on the label' when the real number could be near zero. The offset is also not a constant across seats (it depends on that seat's diagonal/off-diagonal energy split), so cross-seat comparison in Phase 2 is distorted too.
findings.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-curly-octo-goggles/76f53c89-e2a9-52bb-8817-9460fd780b76/scratchpad/audit/pack_read.py: with a random symmetric q=120 matrix packed exactly as `build_mq_label.pack` writes it, `unpack()` output has tril(.,-1) identically zero, and a PERFECT prediction gives e_factor = 0.9848 (closed form sqrt((F^2-D^2)/(F^2+D^2)) = 0.9848, exact match). Substituting the real seat-0253 magnitudes from docs/data/equi_20260918/MQ_RESULT_0253.json gives a floor of 0.283. By contrast train_equi.py:270 and platen.py:37 both do `M + triu(M,1).T` on the same packed layout.
findings.fix: At line 221 symmetrise exactly as line 270 does: `label = unpack(sample['label'], q, dev); label = label + torch.triu(label, 1).T` before computing e_factor (diag_rel on line 223 is unaffected either way). Any SPECTRUM.json already produced by the running A1 arms must have its factor_relative discarded, not reinterpreted.

findings.title: build_mq_label records its numerical self-tests but never gates on them, and prepare() only re-checks read_blocks_roundtrip - a corrupted label ships silently
findings.claim: Of the builder's checks only five raise: the R_UPPER sha (line 79), R upper/positive-diagonal (line 87), rigid shape (line 91), lam.min()<=0 (line 103), diag.min()<=0 (line 139) and read_blocks_roundtrip!=0 (line 168). The four checks that actually establish that M_q is the right matrix -- `MMG_residual` (109), `rigid_nullspace` (123), `round_trip_to_M` (125), `back_squared_times_A_minus_I` (128) and `label_g` (134) -- are written into MQ_RESULT.json and never compared with any tolerance. `train_equi.prepare` (line 102-105) re-checks r_sha256, trace_sha256, m_sha256, q and `read_blocks_roundtrip != 0.0` -- but not label_g, not round_trip_to_M, not rigid_nullspace. This is a regression from the previous route: route5/expand_inverse_labels.py:44 gates `abs(rec['label_g'] - 1) > 1e-8` and `LtLA_minus_I > 1e-9`.
findings.failure_scenario: Phase 2 (handover section 5) builds M_q for 55-95 seats with a loop over `build_mq_label`. A seat whose A is far worse conditioned than seat 0253 (whose A^-1 spans only 28.4 .. 2.05e6, ratio 7.2e4) -- say cond(A) ~ 1e13 -- still passes lam.min() > 0 and diag.min() > 0, but its eigh-based A^{-1/2} carries O(1) relative error in the soft directions. label_g comes out at, e.g., 3.0 instead of 1 + 5e-11. Nothing raises; MQ_RESULT.json is written; train_equi.prepare accepts the seat; the network is trained toward and scored against a corrupted target whose own g is 3.0, so no arm can ever report g < 3.0 for that seat. The multi-geometry arm then looks like the architecture failing again (the exact conclusion section 2.3 is set up to draw), and nobody re-reads 95 JSON files to find the one bad label.
findings.evidence: Read of build_mq_label.py lines 96-146: the only `raise` statements between the eigh and the pack are on lam.min() and diag.min(). Read of train_equi.py lines 102-105: the MQ receipt condition is `mq['r_sha256'] != ... or mq['trace_sha256'] != ... or mq['m_sha256'] != sha256(label) or int(mq['q']) != q or mq['read_blocks_roundtrip'] != 0.0` -- label_g does not appear. Contrast route5/expand_inverse_labels.py:44. My numpy mirror of build() (scratchpad/audit/mem.py) reproduces the healthy values (MMG 8.7e-15, rigid 1.6e-17, round_trip 1.1e-16, label_g-1 2.4e-14), confirming these are tight quantities with an obvious threshold available.
findings.fix: In `build()`, after line 134, raise unless `abs(label_g - 1) <= 1e-8`, `round_trip_to_M <= 1e-12`, `MMG_residual <= 1e-12`, `back_squared_times_A_minus_I <= 1e-9` and `rigid_nullspace <= 1e-12` (all five are already 3+ orders of magnitude inside these on seat 0253). Mirror the label_g gate in `train_equi.prepare` alongside the existing read_blocks_roundtrip check, as route5 did.

findings.title: Nothing binds MQ_UPPER.npy to the trace cache it was lifted with, and every builder self-test is blind to a wrong quotient
findings.claim: `build()` checks `sha256(R_UPPER.npy) == receipt['factor_sha256']` (line 78-80) but never checks `sha256(cache_path) == receipt['trace_sha256']`, even though the reference receipt carries that field (the frozen run.py:52 writes it and train_equi.prepare:99-101 uses it). The trace cache is what supplies `rigid` and `order`, i.e. B. Because every self-test after the lift uses the SAME B (`back = Qt(Qt(Mq).T)`, `Mq @ rigid`, `label_g` via `back`), all of them are identities in B and pass exactly for ANY valid rigid trace. So the builder reports a flawless label while writing a completely different matrix. `--trace-cache` defaults to `<reference>/input/TRACE_CACHE.npz` (line 77), and handover section 3.3 explicitly instructs passing the manifest's `trace_cache` field by hand for V2 seats -- the exact place a mispairing happens. `platen.py` (the Phase-3 observable) takes `--mq` and `--trace-cache` as independent arguments with no binding check at all.
findings.failure_scenario: Build seat X's M_q with seat Y's TRACE_CACHE.npz (wrong --trace-cache, or a stale copy under <reference>/input/). MQ_RESULT.json reports MMG 3.6e-15, rigid_nullspace 3.8e-17, round_trip_to_M 2.5e-16, back^2 A - I 2.5e-14, label_g - 1 = 4.8e-14 -- indistinguishable from a correct build -- while MQ_UPPER.npy differs from the correct label by 50 % relative. In train_equi this is caught late, by prepare's receipt comparison. In the Phase-3 plan of handover section 5 it is NOT caught: `platen.py --mq <MQ_PRED_UPPER.npy> --trace-cache <PATH_k cache> --q 12798` is run five times pairing one checkpoint's predictions with five different caches, and a mispairing silently yields a wrong d(trace H^-1)/d eps against the teacher value -2.278.
findings.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-curly-octo-goggles/76f53c89-e2a9-52bb-8817-9460fd780b76/scratchpad/audit/wrongB.py, which builds A and R from quotient B_A and then runs the builder's exact sequence twice, once with B_A and once with a B from a different node geometry: 'right cache  MMG=3.6e-15 rigid_nullspace=3.4e-17 round_trip_to_M=1.9e-16 back^2A-I=2.4e-14 label_g-1=4.9e-14' / 'WRONG cache MMG=3.6e-15 rigid_nullspace=3.8e-17 round_trip_to_M=2.5e-16 back^2A-I=2.5e-14 label_g-1=4.8e-14 ... but the LABEL itself differs from the right one by 0.498 relative'.
findings.fix: In `build()`, next to the r_sha check, add `if sha256(cache_path) != receipt['trace_sha256']: raise ValueError('FROZEN_TRACE_BINDING')`. In `platen.py`, require the reference directory (or the MQ_RESULT.json next to --mq) and assert its `trace_sha256` equals sha256(--trace-cache) and its `q` equals --q, instead of trusting three free-form arguments.

findings.title: Three of the builder's recorded self-tests cannot fail: packed_symmetry_exact, the tril(R,-1) assertion, and sym_residual_before_average is None
findings.claim: (a) Line 170 `packed_symmetry_exact = np.array_equal(Mh, Mh.T)` is a tautology: Mh comes from `Mq = (Mq + Mq.T) * .5` (line 118), and IEEE addition is exactly commutative, so the result is bit-for-bit symmetric always. (b) Line 87's `torch.tril(R, -1) != 0` can never fire, because `unpack` (line 45-49) writes only `out[row, row:]` and leaves the strict lower triangle as the zeros it allocated; only the `R.diagonal() <= 0` half of that assertion is live. (c) Line 122 sets `sym_residual_before_average = None` with the comment 'exact symmetry is checked after packing' -- but the post-pack check is (a), the tautology, so the asymmetry of the raw B^T M B is never measured anywhere. This is low severity because a broken lift would still be caught by round_trip_to_M -- except that finding #2 shows round_trip_to_M is itself never gated.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader of MQ_RESULT_0253.json sees 'packed_symmetry_exact: true' and concludes the packing and the lift were verified symmetric. Neither was: the value is true for any input whatsoever, including a garbage Mq. Likewise 'REFERENCE_IS_NOT_UPPER_WITH_POSITIVE_DIAGONAL' advertises a check on R's lower triangle that unpack has already destroyed the evidence for -- if R_UPPER.npy were ever written in a lower-triangular convention, unpack would silently read its packed entries as an upper triangle and this guard would not notice.
findings.evidence: Measured in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-curly-octo-goggles/76f53c89-e2a9-52bb-8817-9460fd780b76/scratchpad/audit/mem.py: `(X+X.T)*.5 bitwise symmetric: True` for a random float64 X. Measured in scratchpad/audit/pack_read.py: `unpack() of a symmetric packed label is strictly upper-triangular: True`, i.e. tril(.,-1) is identically 0 by construction.
findings.fix: Record the real quantity before symmetrising: `report['sym_residual_before_average'] = float((Mq - Mq.T).norm() / Mq.norm())` immediately before line 118, and gate it (<= 1e-12). Drop `packed_symmetry_exact` or replace it with a check that the packed file round-trips to a symmetric dense matrix through an independent unpacker. Move the R lower-triangle check into `unpack` itself (verify the file's declared convention) rather than after the zero-fill.

findings.title: build() holds ~7 simultaneous q x q float64 buffers; 9.2 GB at q=12828 and 22.4 GB at q=20000
findings.claim: The peak is not the 1.3 GB of one q x q matrix. Measured peak working set for the exact operation sequence of `build()` is 7.0 x (q^2 * 8 bytes). The two peaks are (i) line 114-118, where R, M, half (q,d), half.T.contiguous() (d,q) and the lift's three internal (q,q) buffers (y_old, the outer-product temp `2*v[:,None]*(v@y)[None,:]`, y_new in `RigidQuotient.lift`) are live at once, and (ii) lines 124-128, where R, M, Mq, the `.contiguous()` copy, the forward pass's three internal buffers, A = R.T@R, eye and the two temps of `back @ (back @ A)` overlap. That is 9.2 GB at q=12828 and 22.4 GB at q=20000, plus a further q^2*8 on the host for `Mh = Mq.cpu().numpy()`.
findings.failure_scenario: q=20000 on the 32 GB card: 22.4 GB fits only if the GPU is otherwise empty. Handover section 2.4 records that concurrent label building at 16-21 GB per seat caused 18 consecutive CUDA OOMs and evicted the other jobs; the same section tells the next operator to restart bulk label building once >= 22 GiB is free, which is exactly the boundary and leaves no headroom for the host-side copy or for an A1 evaluation. On CPU, the Phase-2 suggestion to run '2-3 processes in parallel' costs 3 x 9.2 = 27.6 GB at q=12828 (safe under the 90 GiB cgroup) but 3 x 22.4 = 67 GB at q=20000, which together with the page cache the training arms rely on (handover pitfall 4) will push the cgroup over.
findings.evidence: Instrumented numpy mirror of build() at q=2700 with a /proc/self/statm sampler (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-curly-octo-goggles/76f53c89-e2a9-52bb-8817-9460fd780b76/scratchpad/audit/mem.py): 'U=q^2*8=55.6 MB, peak RSS above baseline = 390.2 MB = 7.02 x U'. Scaling: q=12828 -> 7.02 x 1.316 GB = 9.2 GB; q=20000 -> 7.02 x 3.20 GB = 22.5 GB.
findings.fix: Free what is dead before the peaks: `del R` is not possible (it is needed at line 128-130) but `A = R.T @ R` can be computed in place of `eye` via `back @ (back @ (R.T @ R))` chunked, and `M` can be dropped before line 124 by recomputing round_trip_to_M against the packed file. The cheapest single win is to do the lift as `Mq = Qt.lift(Qt.lift(M).T.contiguous())` with `M` deleted first (saves 1 x q^2) and to replace `torch.eye(d)` with a diagonal subtraction. Failing that, document the 7 x q^2 * 8 figure next to the '16-21 GB per seat' note so the next operator does not schedule a q=20000 build alongside anything.

rounds.notes:
Verified CORRECT (no finding), with runnable evidence in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-curly-octo-goggles/76f53c89-e2a9-52bb-8817-9460fd780b76/scratchpad/audit/:

1. The canonicality claim is TRUE, algebraically and numerically (mq_math.py). With B having orthonormal rows and ker B = span(rigid): (Pi S Pi)^+ = B^T A^-1 B exactly (since B(B^T A B)B^T = A and B^T A^-1 B . B^T A B = Pi), and its PSD square root is B^T A^{-1/2} B because B^T V has orthonormal columns. Measured ||M_q - ((Pi S Pi)^+)^{1/2}|| / ||M_q|| = 8.2e-14. Basis independence: for any orthogonal U, B' = UB gives A' = UAU^T but M_q' = B^T U^T (UAU^T)^{-1/2} U B = M_q; measured ||A-A'||/||A|| = 0.89 while ||M_q - M_q'||/||M_q|| = 3.8e-15. A genuinely different Householder quotient (different elimination order on the same rigid trace) also reproduces M_q to 4.4e-15. Two such B always differ by an orthogonal U = B'B^T, so this covers every admissible B. On the rigid nullspace M_q N = B^T A^{-1/2} B N = 0 exactly (measured 4.7e-17). The construction does require A = B S B^T to be PD, i.e. S PD on ran(Pi); that IS enforced, twice -- R must exist as an upper Cholesky with positive diagonal (line 87) and lam.min() > 0 after the eigh (line 103), both of which raise rather than repair.

2. The packed layout and the reuse of the UNCHANGED reader are sound (pack_read.py). packed_indices(row,col,q) over the q x q upper triangle is a bijection onto [0, q(q+1)/2), matching build_mq_label.pack row-by-row exactly; read_blocks(packed, r, c, q) reproduced Mh[3r+a, 3c+b] masked by lr>=lc to 0.0 absolute error. Indexing by q (not d) is correct: read_blocks' bound check is rows < d//3, which with d=q is the node count q//3, and the "L = R^T" comment is consistent because for a SYMMETRIC M_q the lower entry equals the stored upper one. The diagonal-block mask keeps 6 of 9 entries, and I verified the discarded 3 are recovered exactly by symmetry (block + tril(block,-1)^T reproduces the full symmetric block to 0.0), so no independent entry of M_q is lost. The DOF layout assumption 3*node + component is the frozen one (adapter.py:61 `expected = (3*scalar_order[:,None] + np.arange(3)).ravel()`), and context.py:102 re-checks it.

3. The spectral identity is right. nu = eig((B M_q B^T R^T)^T (B M_q B^T R^T)) = eig(R M^2 R^T) and mu = eig(R^-T A_hat R^-1) = eig((R M^2 R^T)^-1) = 1/nu, so label_g = max(1/nu_min, nu_max) is exactly max_i max(mu_i, 1/mu_i). The `R.T` (not `R`) of handover pitfall 7.2 is used correctly in both build_mq_label.py:130 and train_equi.py:231. mu = (1/nu).flip(0) in evaluate leaves mu ascending, so mu_min = mu[0] / mu_max = mu[-1] are right.

4. `M = (V * lam.sqrt()) @ V.T` is the right associativity (V scaled column-wise by sqrt(lam), then times V^T) and loses nothing: cond(A^-1) = 2.048e6 / 28.36 = 7.2e4 on seat 0253, and the square root halves that to ~269, so the eigh route is comfortably accurate -- the builder's own MMG_residual of 7.6e-15 and label_g - 1 of 4.9e-11 confirm it. My numpy mirror reproduced the same magnitudes.

5. The sha binding chain itself is complete for the train_equi path: prepare() re-derives factor_sha256 and trace_sha256 from the files, compares both with the reference receipt, then requires MQ_RESULT.json's r_sha256, trace_sha256 and m_sha256 to agree and q to match. MQ_RESULT.json is written last (after pack and after the sha of the written file), so a build that dies mid-pack leaves a stale receipt whose m_sha256 no longer matches and prepare raises. The gaps are the two reported above: nothing gates label_g (#2) and build itself never binds the trace cache (#3).

6. platen.py:37 and train_equi.py:270 both symmetrise the packed label correctly (`M + triu(M,1).T`); only train_equi.py:221 does not, which is finding #1. platen.py's `S = B^T A B` is legitimately the full Schur operator here, because S already has the rigid nullspace so Pi S Pi = S -- consistent with the 2.0e-13 agreement with the teacher's six compliances in PLATEN_LABEL_0253.json.

Not examined (other dimensions): model.py's equivariance tables, cubic_group.py's group algebra, the U-Net, the loss, sens_model.py and floor_probe.py.

findings.title: canonical() returns one frame for a tau with a non-trivial stabiliser, so --canonical is not frame-stable and its rotation_consistency probe reads as non-equivariance
findings.claim: `canonical(corners)` returns a single element g* plus the stabiliser size `ties`, but when `ties > 1` there is no canonical frame — only a canonical coset. `train_equi.view_frame` (train_equi.py:203-208) composes `COMPOSE[g_c, g_applied]`, and when the stabiliser is non-trivial that composite is NOT constant in g_applied: the model is shown the same corner vector but a node cloud rotated by a stabiliser element. Nothing in `canonical`, `context.canonical_frame` or `train_equi` warns or raises on ties > 1; `canonical_ties` is recorded in INPUTS.json and then never checked.
findings.failure_scenario: An AFFINE-thickness seat (tau depends on one axis only), corners = [.1,.1,.1,.1,.3,.3,.3,.3] — the handover's Task #25 says 144 such seats exist in V2_LABELS.json. Run `train_equi --canonical` on it. `canonical` gives g*=4, ties=8. The eval probe then evaluates `view_frame(sample, g, canonical=True)` for random g and gets 8 DISTINCT frames {4,5,6,7,12,13,14,15} instead of one. The corners fed to the network are byte-identical across all 8, but pos/faces/node_vector/volume are rotated by a stabiliser element, so the (non-equivariant) network returns a different M and PROBES.json `rotation_consistency` comes out O(0.1-0.3) rather than 0. HANDOVER_EQUI_20260918.md §4 states 'canonical 臂 rotation_consistency ≈ 0 是构造保证', so a reader compares that number against the augment arm's <1e-2 gate and concludes the canonicalisation is broken or the model is badly non-equivariant, when in fact the frame was never unique. Seat 253 is NOT affected (ties=1, single frame g=25), so the three arms running now are safe; the trap is latent for the Phase-2 multi-geometry canonical run.

findings.title: canonical() is discontinuous in tau: a 1e-16 change in one corner moves the canonical corner vector by 2e-2 (~17% relative) whenever two corners are (nearly) equal
findings.claim: `best = max(range(ORDER), key=lambda g: tuple(images[g]))` is a lexicographic max. Contrary to the intuition that a max of continuously varying vectors is continuous, lex-max is discontinuous at PREFIX ties: two images can agree in the leading entries and differ later, and an arbitrarily small perturbation of one corner then swaps the winner and changes the tail of the canonical vector by an O(1) amount. The docstring names the discontinuity in one clause but nowhere is its size stated, and HANDOVER_EQUI_20260918.md §5 (Phase 3, tau-derivative test) and §5 Phase 2 never mention it.
findings.failure_scenario: corners = [.30,.10,.12,.11,.30,.13,.14,.15] (two corners exactly equal, which is the norm for AFFINE/near-symmetric seats). canonical gives g*=41, canon=[0.30,0.30,0.14,0.12,0.13,0.10,0.15,0.11]. Add 1e-16 to corners[0] and canonical gives g*=40, canon=[0.30,0.30,0.12,0.14,0.10,0.13,0.11,0.15] — entries 2..7 change by 0.02, ~17% of the value. Under `--canonical` the network is therefore asked to fit a function of tau that is discontinuous, and two physically indistinguishable geometries land in frames that differ by a finite rotation. Separately, if a future tau-derivative test perturbs corners NON-uniformly around a symmetric baseline, the +h and -h legs take different frames (I measured g+=13 vs g-=15 for corners=[.1,.1,.1,.1,.3,.3,.3,.3] with a random direction v) and the central difference returns the average of two different one-sided derivatives, not a derivative of anything.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-curly-octo-goggles/76f53c89-e2a9-52bb-8817-9460fd780b76/scratchpad/audit/t2.py, sections 5c and 5d, output above. Also quantified the safe margin for the seats in play: for seat 253's real corners a per-corner uniform(-h/2,h/2) jitter flips the frame 0/200 times at h=1e-3 and 85/200 times at h=1e-2. IMPORTANT MITIGATION I verified: the Phase-3 perturbation is NOT per-corner — superelement/objective/tau_gate.py:3 says the five seat-0328 operators are 'tau_corners scaled by 1+eps'. A uniform positive scale is exactly lex-order preserving, so the canonical frame is provably constant along that path; I confirmed it stays g*=25 for seat 253 and stays constant for all tied/constant/affine test vectors at eps in {0,+-1e-4,+-1e-3}, and over scales 1e-9..1e9 for signed corners. So Phase 3 as specified is safe; the exposure is Phase 2 and any later per-corner design perturbation.
findings.fix: Either state the constraint explicitly where it is consumed (a note in the handover Phase 2/Phase 3 sections plus a PROTOCOL field recording the lex-margin `canon[0] - second-largest image[0]` per seat), or replace the lex-max tie-break with a smooth-invariant canonicalisation. At minimum have `canonical` also return the winning margin so a run can flag seats where the frame is decided by less than, say, 1e-6, and refuse `--canonical` on them.

For nodes (top=2n): map_int_positions(u,g,2n)/2n equals map_positions(u/2n,g) to 0.0 for n in {1,2,4,8,16,32} over the full (2n+1)^3 grid and all 48 g. For CELL CENTRES (top=n-1): I derived it from first principles — 2u-top = 2n(p-1/2) exactly when p=(i+1/2)/n, so the map is the correct conjugation of Q about p=1/2 — and confirmed numerically that (map_int_positions(cells,g,n-1)+.5)/n equals map_positions((cells+.5)/n,g) to 5.6e-17 for n in {1,2,3,4,5,8,9,16,32} and all 48 g, with the image always a permutation of the n^3 cell set. Sanity check: top=n, n+1 and 2n all give the WRONG map, so the n-1 choice is load-bearing and right. The parity argument holds because 2u-top has the parity of top entrywise and a signed permutation preserves entrywise parity. Minor doc nit only (not reported as a finding): the docstring "integer coordinates u = top * p" is false for the cell-centre call (u=i, not (n-1)(i+1/2)/n); the arithmetic is still right because only (2u-top) is used.

(2) CORNER_PERM / permute_corners — image convention, and consistent. CORNER_PERM[g][c] is verified to equal the index of map_int_positions(CORNER_BITS[c],g,1) for all 48x8. The scatter out[..., CORNER_PERM[g]] = corners implements tau'(g·c)=tau(c), i.e. the corner vector of the rotated geometry. Composition permute_corners(permute_corners(x,h),g) == permute_corners(x,COMPOSE[g,h]) holds for all 48x48 with 0 mismatches (the selftest only checks the weaker CORNER_PERM[INVERSE[g]][CORNER_PERM[g]] == arange). model.GroupTables uses the identical scatter (corners[corner_perm[g]] = ctx['corners']), and context.py's compile_from_points uses the same 4bx+2by+bz bit order as trilinear's np.ndindex(2,2,2), so nothing drifts.

(3) FACE_PERM — same scatter convention, verified. FACE_NORMALS is [-e0,-e1,-e2,+e0,+e1,+e2] = [x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1], matching context.py's faces = concat((u==0),(u==top)). FACE_PERM[g][f] is the index of Q·n_f for all 48x6; permute_faces composition holds for all 48x48 with 0 mismatches.

(4) cell_source_index / rotate_scalar_volume / rotate_vector_volume — gather direction correct (src[image(k)]=k, so rotated[image(k)]=volume[k]); composition verified for ALL 48x48 pairs, for both scalars and VECTORS, at n=2,3,4,5, exact (rtol=atol=0). The ndindex/ravel_multi_index C-order matches context.py's meshgrid(indexing='ij') volume layout, and context.py's own selftest independently confirms rotate_scalar_volume/rotate_vector_volume against recomputing the volume of the rotated geometry (worst 4.88e-15).

(6) node_permutation — the searchsorted guard is sound. Over an asymmetric boundary-node subset it raised ROTATED_NODE_SET_IS_NOT_THE_NODE_SET for 47/48 g (identity correctly succeeded) with 0 silent-wrong returns. The out-of-range case (single node (0,0,0) under point inversion -> (4,4,4)) hits the `pos.max() >= len(key)` branch and raises cleanly rather than IndexError, because Python's `or` short-circuits before key[order][pos]. The documented convention u_int[pi[i]] == map(u_int[i]) is exact, and I verified the Task-#25 operator action S -> (P_g (x) Q_g) S (...)^T built from it satisfies the group law for all 48x48. Only gap: duplicate node rows would return a non-injective "permutation" silently (pi=[2,2,0,0]) — but compile_equi_inputs derives u_int from one background node per functional with a centroid binding, so duplicates are a teacher-side impossibility; not reported.

(7) Reflections — nothing assumes det=+1. Restricted to the 24 improper elements, tau/phi/grad-tau/grad-phi consistency is 4.44e-15; the isotropic elasticity tensor C(E=1,nu=0.3) is invariant under all 48 Q to exactly 0.0, so "rotated label = Q M Q^T" is as valid for reflections as for rotations. rotate_blocks (einsum 'ab,...bc,dc->...ad') is Q B Q^T and matches model.GroupTables.rotate_blocks.

Cross-cutting end-to-end check: I built a synthetic but strictly covariant nodal rank-2 operator from geometry alone (distance-weighted dd^T + tau_i*tau_j*I + sym(grad_tau_i grad_phi_j^T) + face-count term) on a 230-node trace and confirmed M(rotate_context(ctx,g)) == rotate_blocks(M(ctx),g) to 2.2e-16 for all 48 g, and to 1.3e-15 when the rotated context is recompiled from scratch instead of rotated. This couples rotate_context to rotate_blocks and would catch any sign/axis flip between the two, which is exactly the convention the augment arm's (input, label) pairing depends on.

One thing that happens to be right and is worth recording: the conditioning statistics (pivot_log_mean/std, diagonal_lower_rms) are calibrated on the UNROTATED label but are exactly rotation invariant here, because all 48 elements are signed permutations — Q B Q^T permutes the 3 diagonal entries among themselves and the 3 off-diagonal magnitudes among themselves. If the group were ever widened beyond signed permutations this would silently break.

Group plumbing: 48 distinct elements, Q Q^T = I, element 0 is the identity, COMPOSE/INVERSE agree with index_of(Q_g Q_h) for all 48x48, |PROPER| = 24, and compose(g,h)="first h then g" matches the row-vector convention of rotate_vectors. GroupTables is built with a single n guarded by `any(s['ctx']['n'] != n)`, so cell_source_index is never called with the wrong n.

findings.title: `--canonical` is not a unique frame when the tau corner vector has a non-trivial stabiliser, so the canonical arm's rotation_consistency is not ~0 "by construction"
findings.claim: `canonical_frame`/`cubic_group.canonical` pick the *first* lexicographic maximiser of the permuted corner vector. When the stabiliser of the canonical corner vector has size s>1, the composed frame `COMPOSE[g_c(h), h]` takes s distinct values as h ranges over the 48 elements, so the cell is presented to the network in s different orientations, not one. The returned `ties` is recorded (`train_equi.py:122`, `canonical_ties`) but never gated on, and `context.selftest` hard-asserts `ties == 1` (line 184), so the s>1 branch is never exercised anywhere.
findings.failure_scenario: Phase 2 (HANDOVER §5) trains/evaluates on the V2 manifest, which contains 144 `thickness=="AFFINE"` seats. Take any seat whose tau is affine in one axis only, e.g. corners = [.18,.18,.18,.18,.26,.26,.26,.26] (tau depends on bx alone). `cubic_group.canonical` returns g0=4 with ties=8; the 48 values of `COMPOSE[g_c(h),h]` collapse to exactly the 8-element coset {4,5,6,7,12,13,14,15}; and the canonicalised `pos_int` differs elementwise from the base canonical frame for 42 of the 48 h (it agrees only as a set / up to node relabelling). The `--canonical` arm's `PROBES.json:rotation_consistency` on such a seat is therefore the model's residual non-equivariance under the 8-element stabiliser, i.e. NOT ~0. HANDOVER_EQUI_20260918.md §4 ("canonical 臂 rotation_consistency ≈ 0 是构造保证") and §3.5 would make that nonzero number look like a bug in `rotate_context`/`GroupTables`, or like the canonical arm being broken, when it is expected behaviour. The currently running A1 arms are unaffected (seat 253 has canonical_ties=1, evidence docs/data/equi_20260918/SMOKE_INPUTS.json).
findings.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-curly-octo-goggles/76f53c89-e2a9-52bb-8817-9460fd780b76/scratchpad/audit/t4.py: `canonical g0 = 4  stabiliser size (ties) = 8`; `distinct composed frames g_c(h) o h over the 48 h: [4,5,6,7,12,13,14,15] -> count 8`; `stabiliser of canonical corners: [0,1,2,3,8,9,10,11] count 8`; `h for which canonicalised pos_int differs elementwise from the base canonical: 42 of 48`; `corner vectors all identical across h: True`. Also confirmed `context.selftest` line 184 is `assert ties == 1`, and `train_equi.py:394` uses `sample['canonical_g']` with no ties check.
findings.fix: Either (a) make the frame canonical on more than the corners when ties>1 (break the tie with a stabiliser-invariant of the node set, e.g. the lexicographically largest sorted `pos_int` key among the s maximisers), or (b) refuse/flag: raise or set `canonical_frame_unique=False` in PROTOCOL/INPUTS when `ties>1`, and state in the doc that the canonical arm's rotation_consistency probe only tests the stabiliser coset. Minimal version: add `if ties > 1: record['canonical_frame_unique']=False` and a matching sentence in §4's equivariance gate.

findings.title: `compile_equi_inputs` silently ignores `metadata['geometry']['tau_corners']`, while the Phase-3 recipe in the handover tells the operator to set the geometry there
findings.claim: The geometry is taken exclusively from `cache['tau_corners']` (the TRACE_CACHE.npz). `metadata['geometry']` is only read for `representation` and `box_max`; there is no assertion that `cache['tau_corners']` and `metadata['geometry']['tau_corners']` agree, even though the repo keeps both live (`superelement/objective/trace_replay.py:16` builds the case row from the *metadata* copy).
findings.failure_scenario: HANDOVER_EQUI_20260918.md §5 Phase 3 instructs: "INPUT.json 若缺，把 seat 328 的复制到 TRACE_CACHE 旁边，只改 `metadata.geometry.tau_corners`". Editing that field changes nothing in the context. If a PATH_k directory is served with the baseline seat-328 TRACE_CACHE (or any cache whose `tau_corners` is the unperturbed vector) and only the INPUT.json metadata is edited per the recipe, `compile_equi_inputs` returns the *baseline* context for all five eps in {-1e-3,-1e-4,0,+1e-4,+1e-3}. findings.evidence: Read context.py:84-108: the only uses of `metadata` are `geometry.representation`, `geometry.box_max`, `n`, `gp`, `material`; line 108 passes `cache['tau_corners']`. `grep -rn tau_corners superelement/equi superelement/objective` shows context.py uses the cache copy and objective/trace_replay.py:16 uses `sample['geometry']['tau_corners']` — two live sources, no cross-check. findings.fix: In `compile_equi_inputs`, after reading the cache, add `if 'tau_corners' in metadata['geometry'] and not np.allclose(np.asarray(metadata['geometry']['tau_corners'], float), np.asarray(cache['tau_corners'], float), rtol=0, atol=1e-12): raise ValueError('TAU_CORNERS_METADATA_CACHE_MISMATCH')`, and correct §5 Phase 3 to say the perturbed tau must come from each PATH_k's own TRACE_CACHE (`cache['tau_corners']`), not from INPUT.json.

findings.title: `GroupTables.rotate_context` recomputes `pos` in float32 instead of from the exact integer grid; bit-exact only because 2n is a power of two
findings.claim: `context.rotate_context` keeps `pos_int` and sets `pos = pos_int/(2n)` (exact). The torch path drops `pos_int` (`model.to_torch` does not carry it) and recomputes `out['pos'] = (ctx['pos'] - .5) @ Q.T + .5` in float32. That is bit-exact only when 1/(2n) is a dyadic rational representable in float32, i.e. when 2n is a power of two. `train_equi` guards `MIXED_GRID_SIZES` (line 376) but never requires n to be a power of two.
findings.failure_scenario: With n=32 (all current seats) the two paths agree to 0.0, so nothing is wrong today. If a future seat has n=24 or n=25, every rotated node position acquires a 5.96e-08 float32 error relative to the exact integer path. Since `predict_full_q` rotates the context for the probe and un-rotates the blocks, the `rotation_consistency` and `index_shuffle_relative_discrepancy` probes acquire a ~1e-7 floor from input rounding alone, and the "< 1e-2" equivariance gate and the "must vanish" index-shuffle gate would be read against a floor whose origin is not recorded anywhere.
findings.evidence: Ran scratchpad/audit/t3.py over all 48 g on the full (2n+1)^3 node grid: `n=32: max |integer-path pos - (p-.5)Q^T+.5| in float32 = 0.0`; `n=25: 5.9604645e-08`; `n=24: 5.9604645e-08`. model.to_torch (model.py:44-54) omits `pos_int`; train_equi.py:375-377 only rejects mixed n.
findings.fix: Either carry `pos_int` into the torch context and set `pos = pos_int.float()/(2n)` after applying the integer signed permutation, or add an explicit `if (2*n) & (2*n-1): raise ValueError('GRID_NOT_POWER_OF_TWO')` next to the MIXED_GRID_SIZES check so the float32 floor can never appear silently.

findings.title: Volume encoder inputs are unnormalised: 99.0% of the first conv's input variance is a constant field, tau/grad_tau get 0.0024%
findings.claim: `encode` feeds `ctx['volume']` to `self.volume_encoder` raw, while `node_input` (line 209) explicitly divides the SAME field by 2*pi with the comment "grad phi is O(2 pi); keep inputs O(1)". In the volume path phi and grad_phi are left at their natural scale, and phi = sum cos(2 pi p) does not depend on tau at all: 4 of the 10 volume channels (phi, grad_phi[x,y,z]) are BIT-IDENTICAL for every geometry and every seat with the same n, yet they carry 99.03% of the first Conv3d's input variance. The design variable channels (tau, grad_tau) carry 0.0024%, an amplitude ratio of 211:1. GroupNorm after conv1 cannot repair this: it rescales the summed feature map, not the per-channel contributions, so the tau-induced component stays at ~1/211 relative amplitude and its weight gradients are suppressed by the same factor.
findings.failure_scenario: n=32, corners drawn in the seat-0253 range (0.15-0.25): measured per-channel variances are grad_phi[x/y/z] = 19.7392 each (32.19% of the total each), phi = 1.5000 (2.45%), margin = 0.4950 (0.81%), solid = 0.0990 (0.16%), grad_tau = 4e-4..5e-4 (0.00%), tau = 2e-4 (0.00%); total 61.31. Two contexts built on the same node set with corners [0.161 0.235 0.239 0.222 0.244 0.245 0.213 0.203] vs [0.382 0.252 0.198 0.231 0.411 0.128 0.299 0.085] give max|diff| = 0.0 on phi and all three grad_phi channels. The three running seat-0253 arms are NOT affected (tau is frozen, so a tau-blind volume encoder costs nothing). The wrong conclusion arrives in Phase 2 and Phase 3: the multi-geometry arm (the exact test the old architecture failed in HANDOVER section 2.3) asks the volume encoder to distinguish geometries through channels holding 0.97% of its input energy, and Phase 3 asks it for d(trace H^-1)/d eps through channels holding 0.0024%. A poor result would be read as "the new architecture also cannot learn multi-geometry" when the measured cause is input scaling.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-curly-octo-goggles/76f53c89-e2a9-52bb-8817-9460fd780b76/scratchpad/audit/t8.py and t9.py (numpy, real context.compile_from_points on a 32^3 grid). t8 output: 'grad_phi share of first-conv input energy : 96.58 %', 'tau + grad_tau share : 0.0024 %', 'amplitude ratio |grad_phi| : |grad_tau| = 210.9'; node path for comparison: node grad_tau std 0.0372, node grad_phi std raw 3.6327, after /2pi 0.5782. t9 output: phi and grad_phi_{x,y,z} 'bitwise identical across two DIFFERENT geometries: True, max|diff| 0.0000e+00'; tau/margin/solid/grad_tau all False.

The clamp is per-axis and the axis map is a signed permutation, so a node clamped to the x=0 layer rotates to a node clamped to the correspondingly rotated layer; the two PyTorch clamp orderings (clip the unnormalised coordinate, or clip the bilinear corner indices) give the same value at a face because the weights are 0.5/0.5 onto a doubled index. Interior even grid coordinates (u even, 0<u<2n) land between two cell layers with equal weights, and the flip maps that pair to its image pair - also exact. Segment samples CANNOT leave the cell: both endpoints are in the closed unit cube and segment_t is in (0,1), so every sample is a convex combination (measured min 0.0, max 1.0 over 4000 pairs x 8 samples); segment equivariance 3.331e-16 over all 48 g. Axis order (z,y,x) is right: grid[...,0] must index the last array axis, and it carries 2*p[2]-1.

(2) Resampling under the 48 - CLEAN. See finding 4 for the numbers. The full VolumeUNet reimplemented in numpy with O_h-invariant kernels (including GroupNorm and SiLU) is equivariant to 2.93e-15, so avg_pool/nearest-up/zero-pad/GroupNorm contribute nothing to non-equivariance. nearest x2 upsampling commutes with a flip EXACTLY (0.0), because i -> {2i,2i+1} carries the same value into both fine cells. (3) decode's transposition symmetry - CLEAN AND EXACT. A numpy replica of the off-diagonal path gives |B_ij - B_ji^T| = 0.0 and matches an independently constructed 0.5*(f(i,j) + f(j,i)^T)*scale to 0.0. `.reshape(-1,3,3).transpose(1,2).reshape(-1,9)` is the correct 3x3 transpose under row-major packing. `near` is symmetric in (i,j) and is applied to the SAME row index in both halves (row k of `state[:m]` and row k of `state[m:]` are the two orderings of pair k), and `scale` shares that indexing, so the mask/scale pairing is right. findings.fix: Skip the probe when `args.canonical` and `canonical_ties == 1` (write rotation_consistency = 'identically zero by construction: constant view frame' into PROBES.json instead), or, better, make it informative by probing the canonical arm with the 48/|stab| distinct frames a *different* geometry in the same orbit would land in. Either way record `canonical_ties` in PROBES.json so a reader can tell a tautological 0.0 from a measured one.

findings.title: No resume path, 313 un-pruned checkpoints per arm (106 GB across three arms) that the §2.5 resource ledger omits
findings.claim: `--checkpoint-every 64` over 20000 steps writes 313 checkpoints per arm and nothing prunes them; at 116 MB (9.68M params x 4 B x 3 for param + exp_avg + exp_avg_sq) that is 35.5 GB per arm and 106 GB for the three arms, of which ~105 GB is dead weight since nothing in the repository ever loads an equi checkpoint (grep: the only readers of CHECKPOINT_*.pt are route5/head/v0/v1 scripts with their own model classes). `args.output.mkdir(exist_ok=False)` and the absence of any --resume flag mean a crash at step 19000 discards the whole run, and the `near_radius` and `numpy_rng`/`torch_rng` that were saved for resuming are read by nobody. `model.near_radius` is an instance attribute, not a buffer, so it is absent from `state_dict()`; any future loader that only does `load_state_dict(saved['model'])` silently gets the class default 0.0625 (model.py:264) instead of `args.near_cells / n`.
findings.failure_scenario: Concrete loss path: §2.4 plans to restart LABELS95 (43 remaining seats x ~0.66 GB) plus 95 M_q labels (65-90 GB) while the arms are checkpointing. 321 GB free - 106 GB checkpoints - ~28 GB L labels - ~77 GB M_q = 109 GB, i.e. still above the 60 GB floor, so this is a margin loss rather than a certain failure; but if any of those estimates is 50 % low, `torch.save` raises, the `except BaseException` writes FAILURE.json, and 75 minutes x 3 arms of training is unrecoverable because there is no resume. Latent numeric path: Phase 3 (seat 0328) or any run with `--near-cells 3` writes a checkpoint whose near_radius is 0.09375, and a reload that uses only state_dict routes every pair with 0.0625 < |delta| <= 0.09375 through far_head instead of near_head, with the wrong conditioning scale, changing the predicted blocks silently.
findings.evidence: 20000/64 -> steps 64..19968 plus step==20000 = 313 files; 9.68e6 x 3 x 4 B = 110.8 MiB, matching the handover's 116 MB. `superelement/prune_checkpoints.py` already implements the right policy (keep 64*2^k plus the last 3 -> ~12 files, 1.4 GB per arm) but nothing in the handover or the launch scripts runs it. grep for load_state_dict shows no equi loader; grep for near_radius shows it is written at train_equi.py:417 and read nowhere.
findings.fix: Run `prune_checkpoints.py --root $E --apply` once the three arms finish (it explicitly skips CHECKPOINT.tmp, so it is safe while they run). Register near_radius as a buffer (`self.register_buffer('near_radius_t', torch.tensor(...))`) or assert it against the checkpoint's stored value in any future loader, and add a --resume that restores model/optimizer/step/rng from the newest CHECKPOINT_*.pt.

findings.title: The far-pair sampler's rejection loop has no iteration cap, so a large --near-cells hangs the run silently instead of raising like the empty-near-bucket guard does
findings.claim: `while needed:` in `sample_pairs_geometric` retries until it has collected `per_bucket` pairs that are neither diagonal nor near. If every strict-lower pair is within the near radius the keep mask is empty forever, `needed` never decreases, and the process spins in numpy with no output, no timeout and no error. The symmetric case (no near pairs) is guarded loudly by `EMPTY_NEAR_BUCKET` in `prepare` (line 116); the far side has no equivalent.
findings.failure_scenario: `--near-cells 56` or larger with n=32 gives radius >= 1.75 > sqrt(3), the maximum distance between two nodes of the unit cube, so cKDTree returns all 9,139,950 lower pairs as near and the far loop never terminates. The run produces no TRAIN.jsonl, no FAILURE.json, and holds its GPU allocation; on a shared 32 GB card that starves the other three jobs. This is a mis-typed flag, not a plausible physics setting, hence low severity.
findings.evidence: Read of lines 129-140: `keep = (r != c) & ~is_near; code = code[keep][:needed]; needed -= len(code)` with no bound on iterations. audit/h3.py confirms the membership test itself is exact (searchsorted result identical to the geometric truth over 400k draws, 0 mismatches) so the loop is correct whenever a far pair exists.
findings.fix: Precompute `far_count = count*(count-1)//2 - len(near_codes)` in `prepare`, raise `EMPTY_FAR_BUCKET` if it is zero, and cap the while loop at, say, 64 iterations with a raise.

findings.title: --proper-only is silently ignored unless --augment is also given, so PROTOCOL.json can claim proper_only=true for a run that applied no rotation at all
findings.claim: `elements` is built from `args.proper_only`, but `g = int(rng.choice(elements)) if args.augment else (...)`. With `--proper-only` alone every step uses g = 0 while PROTOCOL.json records `proper_only: true, augment: false`. `--proper-only --canonical` is likewise accepted and ignored (only `--augment` with `--canonical` is rejected).
findings.failure_scenario: A fourth arm launched as `--proper-only --steps 20000` to test 'rotations only' trains as a pure identity arm; its PROTOCOL.json says proper_only=true, and its g / rotation_consistency get tabulated in the three-arm comparison as the 24-element augmentation result. The conclusion 'restricting to proper rotations does not help' would be drawn from a run that never rotated anything.
findings.evidence: Lines 385-388 read together: `elements = CG.PROPER if args.proper_only else np.arange(CG.ORDER)` then `g = int(rng.choice(elements)) if args.augment else ...`. Line 341 writes proper_only into PROTOCOL.json unconditionally.
findings.fix: Alongside the existing `AUGMENT_AND_CANONICAL_ARE_ALTERNATIVES` check, raise if `args.proper_only and not args.augment`.

findings.title: The premise of the whole augment arm - that the teacher's Schur operator is exactly O_h-equivariant - is asserted in three docstrings and verified nowhere
findings.claim: The augmentation pairing is algebraically correct (see notes), but it is only a valid (input, label) pair if S(g . geometry) = P S P^T with P = Perm(pi) tensor Q_g, i.e. if the CutFEM cut-cell quadrature and the trace-functional compiler are exactly cube-symmetric. cubic_group.py's own header says 'up to the teacher's own symmetry error, which is measured, not assumed' - but nothing measures it: the check is deferred to handover Task #25. Everything downstream of the measurable part (phi invariance, trilinear tau, the node set mapping to the rotated geometry's node set) is verified to 5e-15 by the local self-tests; the quadrature is not.
findings.failure_scenario: If the teacher breaks O_h symmetry at, say, 1e-3 relative (not 1e-10 as expected), the augment arm spends 20000 steps regressing onto labels that are wrong by 1e-3 in a structured, orientation-dependent way. Its g and its two-cell sensitivity error would then be worse than the identity arm's for a reason having nothing to do with the network, and §4's equivariance gate ('augment rotation_consistency < 1e-2 and g no worse than identity -> augmentation works') would be read as a verdict on augmentation. This is a missing verification for behaviour that is probably correct, hence low severity per the reporting rule.
findings.evidence: Ran audit/h2.py: if S(rotated cell) = P S P^T then M_q(rotated cell) = P M_q P^T to 6.2e-12 over all 48 g (the residual is my own eigh/inverse roundoff), and GroupTables.rotate_target_blocks reproduces read_blocks(P M_q P^T) EXACTLY (0.0) for diagonal and off-diagonal blocks alike. So the code is right conditional on the premise. grep over the repository and the equi self-tests finds no test of ||P_g S P_g^T - S|| / ||S|| for a stabiliser element; handover §5 'Task #25' proposes it as a side experiment.
findings.fix: Run the Task #25 witness before interpreting the augment arm: pick a V2 manifest seat with thickness=='AFFINE' whose 8 tau corners take only two values grouped by one bit (8-element stabiliser), load S from the packet's S_UPPER.npy, and report max over the 8 stabiliser elements of ||P_g S P_g^T - S||_F / ||S||_F with P_g = node_permutation tensor Q_g. That number is the floor on what augmentation or exact equivariance can ever reach and belongs in the A1 comparison table.

rounds.notes:
Verified CORRECT (with the evidence, so the auditor need not re-do it). Scratch scripts: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-curly-octo-goggles/76f53c89-e2a9-52bb-8817-9460fd780b76/scratchpad/audit/h1.py..h4.py.

(1) THE AUGMENTATION PAIRING IS THE RIGHT PAIRING, and no node permutation is needed. Written out: the rotated cell's node i sits at g.p_i; its operator, indexed by the SAME i, is P M_q P^T with P = Perm(id) tensor Q_g, i.e. block (i,j) -> Q_g M_q(i,j) Q_g^T with NO index permutation. A permutation enters only if you insist the rotated cell be re-indexed the way the compiler would order it (sorted by background id), which is what cubic_group.node_permutation exists for and which training correctly never uses. Verified in audit/h2.py by building a real M_q = B^T A^{-1/2} B on a group-closed node set: for all 48 g, M_q(rotated cell, built from S_rot = P S P^T and the rotated rigid trace) equals P M_q P^T to 6.2e-12 (my own roundoff); and P(pi,Q) M_q P(pi,Q)^T equals P(pi,I) [P(id,Q) M_q P(id,Q)^T] P(pi,I)^T exactly, i.e. the permutation is a pure relabelling. It rests on two assumptions: (a) the model is index-free - structurally true (no index-derived feature survives in context.py; verified exactly by model.selftest's index_shuffle = 0.0 and by the eval probe, 2.75e-7 in the smoke = float32 noise), and (b) the teacher's S is exactly O_h-equivariant - reported as finding 6, verified nowhere.

(2) rotate_target_blocks IS CORRECT. read_blocks(packed, r, c, q) for r > c returns the FULL 3x3 lower block M_q[3r:3r+3, 3c:3c+3] (all 9 entries valid because lr > lc throughout), and for r == c the lower triangle only - confirmed exactly (np.array_equal) against a numpy port of factors.read_blocks in audit/h1.py. Rotating by Q B Q^T is right even though both nodes move, because the index pairing is unchanged and only the 3x3 tensor indices are acted on. audit/h2.py: the numpy twin of rotate_target_blocks (symmetrise diagonal, einsum Q B Q^T, re-mask) reproduces read_blocks(P M_q P^T, r, c) with worst error 0.0 over all 48 g for both diagonal and off-diagonal pairs. Also: Q_g is a signed permutation matrix, so Q B Q^T is an exact re-signing/permutation of entries - it preserves symmetry bitwise, preserves the positivity of the diagonal block's pivots (they are permuted, (QDQ^T)[a,a] = D[sigma(a),sigma(a)]), and preserves every Conditioning statistic (pivot log multiset, diagonal_lower_rms, per-bucket rms), so calibrating on the unrotated labels is consistent with training on rotated ones.

(3) THE BUCKETS ARE THE SAME PARTITION. calibrate_geometric and the training loop both call sample_pairs_geometric on the same sample dict with the same near_codes; only per_bucket (32768 vs 8192) and the rng differ. The Conditioning field names are legacy: same_patch_rms carries the NEAR rms and cross_patch_rms the FAR rms, matching bucket_loss's scales=(diagonal_block_rms, same_patch_rms, cross_patch_rms) indexed by bucket 0/1/2; CONDITIONING.json records this in its field_map. diagonal_lower_rms = rms[3] (strict lower of diagonal blocks) and diagonal_block_rms = rms[0] (all 9 entries incl. the 3 masked zeros) match frozen factors.calibrate exactly. Near sampling is uniform with replacement over the near-pair list. The far sampler's searchsorted membership test is correct: over 400k draws on a 4276-node seat-253-like set it agreed with the geometric truth in every case (0 mismatches), and the r != c filter excludes the diagonal. One subtle thing I checked and it is fine: 1440 pairs sit EXACTLY on the radius (|delta_int|^2 == 16 with radius = 4/(2n)), cKDTree includes them (<= r) while model.decode re-derives near/far from float32 positions - with n = 32 all positions are k/64, exactly representable, so 0 of 18461 near pairs are misrouted and 0 of 399048 far draws are misclassified. This exactness is contingent on n being a power of two; a non-power-of-two n could split a boundary pair between the loss bucket and the head. No empty bucket for a real geometry (EMPTY_NEAR_BUCKET guards one side; the other is finding 4).

(4) THE SPECTRUM IDENTITY IS RIGHT, INCLUDING R vs R^T. Derived and checked numerically in audit/h1.py: with Mhat = A_hat^{-1/2}, W = (Mhat R^T)^T (Mhat R^T) = R Mhat^2 R^T, so 1/eig(W) = eig((R Mhat^2 R^T)^{-1}) = eig(R^-T Mhat^-2 R^-1) = eig(R^-T A_hat R^-1) = mu. For the exact label the code's route gives g = 1 + 1.1e-7, and mu agrees with the directly formed eig(R^-T A_hat R^-1) to 3.9e-12; using R instead of R^T on the same data gives g = 98325, i.e. the route5 trap is avoided here. The .flip(0) and the ordering are right: eigh returns nu ascending, 1/nu is descending, flip makes mu ascending, so mu_min = mu[0] and mu_max = mu[-1] (verified 'mu ascending? True'). Qt is the quotient MAP (forward = B, d-dim output) and Qt.lift is its adjoint B^T - proven from quotient.py (forward = E_{6:} H P, lift = P^T H^T E^T) and independently confirmed by the recorded label self-test round_trip_to_M = 7.4e-16 and back_squared_times_A_minus_I = 5.9e-12 on the real seat. Qt(Qt(M).T) = B M^T B^T = B M B^T because predict_full_q's M is EXACTLY symmetric, not approximately.

(5) A_PRED_UPPER.npy MATCHES ITS CONSUMERS EXACTLY. train_equi writes cholesky_ex(A_hat, upper=True) packed row-major upper, d = receipt['dimension'] = 12822. sens_model.py:188/unpack_upper uses the identical packing loop and forms `Ahat = U.T @ U`; floor_probe.py:55 does the same for kind 'chol'. Same d, same packing, same A = U^T U convention as R_UPPER. --sqrt-factor /nonexistent.npy is skipped cleanly by sens_model's path.exists() check. One small operational note: if cholesky_ex returns info != 0 the file is simply not written (A_hat_spd: false in SPECTRUM.json) and the handover's §2.1 step 2 command would then fail on a missing file - check A_hat_spd before running it.

(6) predict_full_q's DOUBLE WRITE IS BENIGN AND THE SYMMETRY ASSERTION IS EXACT. The first write puts block[a,b] at (3r+a, 3c+b); the second puts block[b,a] at (3c+b, 3r+a) - the same value at the mirrored slot. For r == c both writes target the same 9 slots with the same values, because the diagonal block was made symmetric before rotation and Q B Q^T of a symmetric B is bitwise symmetric (signed permutation, one nonzero term per entry). No index is duplicated within a single advanced-index assignment. Every (r,c) with r >= c is produced exactly once: the triangular inversion rows = floor((sqrt(8*index+1)-1)/2) is exact for the real size (verified for count = 4276, total = 9,144,226: all 9,144,226 pairs distinct, cols <= rows, rows < count; the float64 sqrt has ~1e-12 slack against a 4.7e-4 gap at the row boundary). So `(M - M.T).abs().max() == 0.0` cannot spuriously fail, and cannot spuriously pass either since every entry is written.

(7) view_frame IS CORRECT. COMPOSE[g,h] = Q_g Q_h ('first h then g'), and permute_corners composes the same way (CORNER_PERM[COMPOSE[g,h]] = CORNER_PERM[g] o CORNER_PERM[h]), so COMPOSE[canonical(permute_corners(c, g_applied)), g_applied] does apply g_applied first and then the canonicalising element. For g_applied = 0 it returns canonical(c) = the cell's own canonical frame (= 25 for seat 253), which is exactly the g used during training for that arm, so training and evaluation present the same frame. For general g_applied the model sees identical inputs (verified over all 48 g for 5 tie-free corner vectors) - which is the point of canonicalisation and also the reason the probe is vacuous (finding 3). The handover's 'should be ~0 by construction' is right.

(8) Checkpoints / resume: finding 3 above.

(9) log_pivot_window = (-20, 20) is a LOUD, correct failure for a softer cell. The window is checked against the min/max of log of M_q's diagonal over the FULL diagonal bucket (bucket 0 takes every node, so it is the true min/max, not a sample), and a cell with any pivot above e^20 = 4.85e8 or below e^-20 raises ValueError('REFERENCE_OUTSIDE_LOG_PIVOT_WINDOW') inside calibrate_geometric, before any training step, and the except BaseException handler writes FAILURE.json and re-raises. That is the right behaviour, because EquiModel's own smooth_interval_bound clamps log pivots asymptotically to the same (-20, 20) and could not represent such a label anyway. Seat 0253's e^2.05..e^7.01 has ~13 e-folds of headroom, so realistically only a pathologically soft cell (M_q diagonal ~5e8, i.e. stiffness ~1e-17) would trip it.

Also checked and fine: device handling with --eval-device cpu (GroupTables and the model stay on the train device, blocks are moved per chunk, label/R/rigid/Qt/eigh all on the eval device); the index_shuffle un-shuffle (permute_nodes gives new k = old pi[k], and back[3*pi[k]+a, 3*pi[l]+b] = Mp[3k+a,3l+b] is the correct inverse); the LR schedule (warmup linear then cosine to min_lr at exactly step == steps); rigid_nullspace_leak uses the symmetric M; e_A uses Astar = R^T R; the holdout guard in selected_rows; the frozen-binding sha checks on R_UPPER, TRACE_CACHE and MQ_UPPER including mq['read_blocks_roundtrip'] == 0.0; diag_rel (correct, since unpack's diagonal is intact); the transposition-symmetric off-diagonal head B_ij = (f(i,j) + f(j,i)^T)/2 and its near/far scale routing matching bucket_loss's per-bucket normaliser. Both locally runnable self-tests pass: cubic_group.py (tau/phi field consistency 4.3e-15) and context.py (rotate_context vs recompile-from-rotated-geometry 4.9e-15 over all 48 g).

findings.title: floor_probe.py weights the compliance error by a_j^2/lambda_j instead of a_j^2*lambda_j, overstating the soft-decile share
findings.claim: `wc = aj.square() / lam` is the wrong weight. `aj = E.T @ x` is built from the *displacement* x (line 151: `xq[name] = quotient(u[dof_A])`), not the load. In load coordinates b = E^T f = lam * aj, so mode j's share of the compliance is b_j^2/lam_j = lam_j * aj_j^2, i.e. exactly the energy weight `w = aj.square()*lam` that the module's own docstring prescribes ("compliance driven by 1/r_j - 1 on the same weights"). Using aj^2/lam misweights every mode by lam^2, and because lam is ascending (softest first) it systematically inflates the soft end. `first_order_compliance_error`, `compliance_error_by_decile`, `top_modes`, `top_contributions` and `top_share_of_total` are all affected.
findings.failure_scenario: d=200, A = E diag(lam) E^T with lam log-spaced over 1e-3..1e2, A_hat = E diag(lam*r) E^T with r = 1+0.25*exp(-j/25) (25% too stiff on the softest modes). For load f0 the exact relative compliance error (f^T A_hat^-1 f - f^T A^-1 f)/(f^T A^-1 f) = -0.11186. With the correct weight w = aj^2*lam the reported first_order_compliance_error is -0.11186 (exact for a mode-diagonal A_hat). The shipped code reports -0.15424, i.e. 38% too large; across five random loads it reports -0.154, -0.173, -0.170, -0.163, -0.175 against truths -0.112, -0.117, -0.123, -0.137, -0.134. The decile attribution is worse: the correct compliance_error_by_decile is [-0.1309, -0.0115, -0.0026, -0.0004, ...] (softest decile = 90.0% of the total) while the code reports [-0.1836, -0.0011, -0.00003, ...] (softest decile = 99.4%). The handover section 4 instructs the next model to read exactly this profile ('94-96% of the load energy is in the softest decile, look at that band'), so the equi A1 arms will be triaged with a soft-end share that is an artefact of the weighting.

Table printed: load/true dc/c / fix(aj^2*lam) / -energy_err / current -> f0 -0.11186 / -0.11186 / -0.12902 / -0.15424. Decile shares: correct 0.9002, current 0.9938. Note `load_energy_by_true_stiffness_decile` (line 168, w = aj^2*lam) is CORRECT; only the compliance branch is wrong.

Everything downstream (compliance_err, contrib, compliance_error_by_decile) then follows unchanged and reproduces the exact relative compliance error for a mode-diagonal A_hat. findings.title: Phase-3 tau derivative is contaminated by the discontinuous `solid` input channel; the artefact is 34x the smooth signal at eps=1e-3
findings.claim: `vol_scalar` channel 3 is the hard indicator `(margin >= 0)`, a 0/1 step function of tau on the n^3 grid. The Phase-3 stencil scales tau_corners by (1+eps) with eps in {-1e-3,-1e-4,0,1e-4,1e-3} (tau_gate.py docstring), so the five contexts differ only in tau — and the only channel that is not an O(eps) smooth perturbation is `solid`, which jumps by whole voxels. A central difference of the network's trace(H^-1) over this stencil therefore divides a step by 2h. The channel is also redundant: it is exactly `vol_scalar[2] >= 0`, asserted by context.selftest line 177.
findings.failure_scenario: seat 253 corners (from docs/data/equi_20260918/SMOKE_INPUTS.json), n=32, 32768 voxels, 3530 solid. Under tau -> (1+eps)tau the number of flipped `solid` voxels is 4 at eps=-1e-3, 0 at eps=-1e-4, 0 at +1e-4, 0 at +1e-3. Relative Frobenius input perturbation per channel at eps=-1e-3: tau 1.00e-3, margin 1.82e-4, grad_tau 1.00e-3, **solid 3.37e-2**. So at h=1e-3 the discontinuous channel moves 34x more than tau and 185x more than margin, and asymmetrically (4 flips on the minus side, 0 on the plus side). The signal being measured is only 2*2.278*h = 4.56e-3 relative in trace(H^-1) at h=1e-3 and 4.56e-4 at h=1e-4. For the h=1e-3 estimate to be within 10% of the teacher's -2.278 the network's output must be insensitive to a 3.4e-2 relative one-sided jump in one of its 10 input channels, i.e. have a local Lipschitz constant below ~0.014 in that channel; no such property is designed, enforced or measured. Concrete wrong conclusion: the handover (line 225) proposes the same h=1e-4 vs h=1e-3 Richardson consistency check the teacher passed at 0.999997. The network's two estimates will disagree, and the disagreement will be attributed to 'the network is not smooth in tau' when the cause is a 0/1 discretised input channel. Seat 328 must be checked separately, but it is the same n=32 background mesh and the teacher's own active-cell count moves 7470/7477/7478/7479/7493 over the same stencil (docs/data/pipeline_20260917/TAU_PATHS.json), so flips are expected there too.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-curly-octo-goggles/76f53c89-e2a9-52bb-8817-9460fd780b76/scratchpad/audit/t3.py, run locally against the real superelement.equi.context.field_values with the real seat-253 corners. Also t2.py: min |margin| over the 32^3 grid is 4.375e-5, #(|margin|<1e-3) = 27, #(|margin|<1e-4) = 3.
findings.fix: Either drop channel 3 (it carries no information beyond channel 2, `margin`), or replace it with a smooth saturating function of margin, e.g. tanh(margin/s) or clip(margin/s,-1,1) with s a fixed fraction of a voxel's |grad phi| step. Whichever is chosen, record per-eps the number of flipped voxels alongside the finite difference so the artefact is visible, and quote the h=1e-4 difference (0 flips for seat 253) rather than h=1e-3.

findings.title: The rigid-nullspace leak is exactly annihilated by B(.)B^T, so `Pi M_q Pi` is a bit-level no-op for everything Phase 2/3 reports
findings.claim: B has orthonormal rows with ker(B) = span(rigid), so B^T B = Pi = I - N(N^T N)^-1 N^T and B Pi = B. Hence B M_q B^T = B (Pi M_q Pi) B^T identically: the part of a predicted M_q_hat that produces the reported `rigid_nullspace_leak` lives entirely in the Pi-complement and is discarded by the sandwich in platen.operator_from_mq (line 40) and in train_equi.evaluate (line 228). It therefore cannot affect Mhat, inv(Mhat), A_hat, mu, g, e_A, A_PRED_UPPER.npy, or any number out of sens_model.py / floor_probe.py / platen.py. The handover's section-4 triage line ('leak > 1e-2 means the network is dumping energy in the rigid directions', line 203) is offered as an explanation for a bad g, and Phase 6 (line 241) prescribes `Pi M_q_hat Pi` 'before assembly'. The Phase-6 use is correct (there M_q_hat is used directly in q space as a preconditioner); the section-4 causal reading, and any application of Pi ahead of the Phase-2/3 measurements, is not.
findings.failure_scenario: q=60 with a 6-dim rigid trace, exact label M_q = B^T A^-1/2 B (leak 4.6e-17). Add a leak L = Pi X Q + (Pi X Q)^T + Q X Q (Q = I-Pi) scaled so the reported metric ||M_q N||_F/(||M_q||_F ||N||_F) becomes 4.93e-3. Then ||B(M_q+L)B^T - B M_q B^T||/||B M_q B^T|| = 4.8e-16, ||B(Pi(M_q+L)Pi)B^T - B(M_q+L)B^T||/||.|| = 5.5e-16, and ||A_hat(leaked) - A_hat||/||A_hat|| = 3.5e-15. So: the next model reads `rigid_nullspace_leak: 1.8e-2` in an A1 SPECTRUM.json, concludes this explains a g worse than route5's 12.75, applies Pi M_q_hat Pi and re-evaluates — and gets a bit-identical g. Three 20000-step arms get triaged down the wrong branch.

The five operators are certified ADMITTED_SAME_TRACE (same q=12798, same order, same quotient), so the five trace caches are interchangeable for the fixture and every run passes every shape check whichever cache is used; the only thing that distinguishes the five outputs is which MQ_PRED_UPPER.npy was passed. findings.title: platen.py omits run.py's trace-fixture guard, so a non-box-only cache yields silent wrong numbers
findings.claim: run.py:112 returns `dict(status='NOT_RUN_GENERAL_SIGNED_TRACE_FIXTURE_REQUIRED')` unless `np.all(np.diff(cache['indptr'])==1) and np.all(cache['coefficients']==1) and np.all(cache['kind']==0)`. platen_response has no such check, yet it depends on the same assumption twice: `end_registry(cache['support_centroid'])` treats support_centroid rows as node positions and builds `prescribed = (3*ids[:,None]+arange(3)).ravel()`, which is only the correct trace-dof layout when each trace functional is one background node with unit coefficient and no residual cut coordinate. Every other consumer of these caches raises loudly (context.compile_equi_inputs:93 BOX_ONLY_TRACE_REQUIRED, :95 ONLY_THE_INERT_CUT_PLANE_IS_SUPPORTED); platen.py is the exception.
findings.failure_scenario: A seat is added whose packet has a general signed trace (a functional that is a combination of background nodes, or a residual cut coordinate). build_mq_label.py has no such guard either, so MQ_UPPER.npy is built; platen.py is then pointed at that cache. `support_centroid` is a weighted centroid rather than a node position, so both the z==0 / z==1 end selection and the 3*node+comp dof mapping are wrong: a wrong set of dofs is clamped, `end_registry`'s rank-6 check on `values` still passes (the rigid fields of any 3+ scattered points are rank 6), `force_response`'s symmetry and equilibrium checks still pass (they only involve the 6x6 H), and trace(H^-1) and the 18 compliances come out finite, plausible and wrong. In the same situation run.py would report NOT_RUN.
findings.evidence: run.py:111-113 versus platen.py:47-56; response.py:18-35 (end_registry builds prescribed dofs as 3*ids+arange(3) from the points array it is given); context.py:93 shows the guard the rest of the new package enforces.
findings.fix: Copy run.py's guard into platen_response (or platen.main) and raise, e.g. `if not (np.all(np.diff(cache['indptr'])==1) and np.all(cache['coefficients']==1) and np.all(cache['kind']==0)): raise ValueError('BOX_ONLY_TRACE_REQUIRED')`. Consider the same in build_mq_label.build.

findings.title: platen.py's `free_equilibrium_relative` is a weaker quantity than run.py's field of the same name
findings.claim: run.py builds the free-equilibrium residual from `force = F.full_action(R, Q, u)` (line 126) while the right-hand side came from the dense lifted `S` (line 120). The residual therefore cross-checks the dense sandwich S = B^T A B against the factored action B^T R^T R B: a wrong transpose in the lift would show up there. platen.py uses `S @ u` for both `rhs` (line 56) and `force` (line 63), so `residual` reduces algebraically to the Cholesky back-substitution residual of the block it just solved and is ~1e-14 no matter whether S is the right matrix. The field keeps run.py's name, so its value will be compared to run.py's RESPONSE.json values as if it certified the same invariant.
findings.failure_scenario: Suppose S were built with a misplaced transpose (a plausible slip given run.py's and platen.py's nested lift-transpose-lift-transpose expression). platen.py would solve S'u=0 self-consistently and still report free_equilibrium_relative ~5e-14, while run.py's residual on the same operator would blow up. The 4.9e-14 in docs/data/equi_20260918/PLATEN_LABEL_0253.json is therefore not evidence that platen's fixture is right; only the --compare max_relative_compliance_difference of 2.0e-13 against run.py's independently-computed reference response is.
findings.evidence: run.py:120 `rhs=-(S@u)[i]` / :126 `force=F.full_action(R,Q,u)` / :127 residual, versus platen.py:56 / :63 / :64. Verified with the numpy port that the two force computations agree mathematically: ||S@u - full_action(R,Q,u)||_max / ||full_action||_max = 4.3e-15 (t1.py), so the substitution is correct — it just removes the cross-check.
findings.fix: Either rename the field (e.g. `solve_residual_relative`) so it is not compared to run.py's, or restore the cross-check: platen has no factored operator, so the cheap equivalent is to assert once that `Qt.lift(Qt(A @ Qt(u)))` (or `Qt.lift(A @ Qt(u))`) matches `S @ u` to ~1e-12 before reporting.

- Memory/shape safety: unpack raises FP64_UPPER_REQUIRED on a wrong --q, and RigidQuotient.forward/lift raise on any q mismatch with the cache, so a mismatched --q/--mq/--cache triple cannot silently run (only a same-q mispairing can — see the provenance finding).

Question 2 (the 2.0e-13 claim) — the comparison is against the right object.
run.py:188-196 writes RESPONSE.json as {predicted, reference, comparison, ...} where `reference = six_response(reference, sample)` and `reference` is R_UPPER (the teacher's Cholesky factor) for every head, not the prediction. So platen.py:86 `json[...]['reference']` is the teacher. docs/data/equi_20260918/PLATEN_LABEL_0253.json confirms it compared against .../S1_LOGPIVOT/EVAL_0253/RESPONSE.json and got max_relative_compliance_difference = 2.045e-13, with reference_trace_H_inverse 6027.614615326554 against platen's own 6027.614615326934 (6e-14 relative).
What the 2e-13 does establish: the MQ_UPPER packing and platen's unpack/symmetrise; B M_q B^T = A^{-1/2} and the inverse-square recovering A; and cross-implementation agreement between platen's dense-S fixture and run.py's factored-action fixture. What it does NOT establish: anything about response.py/end_registry/force_response themselves (common-mode to both sides of the comparison) and anything about a prediction. So the handover's wording ('this M_q -> A_hat -> physics path is validated independently of the network') is literally accurate and not circular, with two caveats worth fixing in the prose only: it is a round-trip/consistency check rather than an accuracy claim, and 'the six compliances' is 18 load columns spanning a 6-dimensional load space (response.force_dictionary: 6 unit resultants + 12 mixed force/moment combinations; response.py itself labels this 'specified physical load span only; not complete trace spectrum').

Question 3 (sens_model.py compatibility) — correct object, correct dimension.
`--chol-factor` wants a packed upper triangle (length d(d+1)/2, float64) of an upper-triangular U with A_hat = U^T U, in the frozen quotient, dimension d = q-6 (sens_model.py:34-43, :188-190, d from V.Label). train_equi.evaluate:258-261 writes exactly that (`cholesky_ex(Ahat, upper=True)` then pack of the upper triangle of the d x d factor), and route5/eval_inverse.py:120-129 writes the same object under the same name, so 'chol' is right for both. The two-cell assembly needs the d x d QUOTIENT operator, not the q x q trace operator: sens_model.dense_S lifts it internally to S = B^T A_hat B before scattering into K on 3*N_nodes dofs. d = 12822, q = 12828 for seat 253 (MQ_RESULT_0253.json, SMOKE_INPUTS.json) — consistent. `worst_compliance_rel` = max over the 4 loads of |c_pred - c_exact|/|c_exact|; `worst_sensitivity_rel` = max over loads and the two modules of |dc/drho_m error|/|exact|; both against A = Rstar^T Rstar on identical loads, no repair. The handover's step-2 command (`--sqrt-factor /nonexistent.npy`) is handled by the `path.exists()` skip at line 185. The adjoint identity gate |sum_m dc/drho_m + c|/|c| <= 1e-8 (line 178) is self-validating and legitimately holds despite the rank-6 `K.addmm_(Nrb,Nrb.T,alpha=sc)` regulariser, because both f and u are projected off Nrb.
Cross-check available: train_equi's mu (1/eig((Mhat R^T)^T(Mhat R^T)), train_equi.py:231-240) and sens_model's eps_op_of (eig(R^-T A_hat R^-1), lines 158-166) are the same spectrum, so mu_min/mu_max in SPECTRUM.json and SENS_MODEL.json must agree for each arm — worth asserting when the arms land.

Question 4 (floor_probe --arms / build_Ahat) — 'chol' is right.
`--arms name:kind:path` splits on ',' then `split(':',2)`; the handover's two-arm string parses correctly (no ':' or ',' in these paths). build_Ahat kind 'chol' does U.T @ U, which is the correct inverse of how both train_equi and eval_inverse pack A_PRED_UPPER. 'sqrt' (U + triu(U,1).T then M@M) is for M_PRED_UPPER-style symmetric roots and must NOT be used here. `load_energy_by_true_stiffness_decile` (w = aj^2*lam) is correct; only the compliance branch is not (see finding 1).

Question 5 (canonical frame) — NOT a hazard for this stencil, quantified for others.
The Phase-3 perturbation is a positive scaling tau -> (1+eps)tau (tau_gate.py docstring, confirmed by TAU_PATHS.json). cubic_group.canonical picks the lexicographic argmax over the 48 permuted corner vectors, and lexicographic order is invariant under multiplication by a positive scalar, so g* is provably constant across the stencil. Verified numerically on seat 253's real corners: g*=25, ties=1 at all five eps (matches SMOKE_INPUTS canonical_frame=25, canonical_ties=1). Quantification for other perturbation shapes: the smallest ADDITIVE single-corner shift that switches seat 253's g* is 1.709e-3 (corners 5 and 6), and over 2000 random unit directions in 8-dim corner space the minimum critical magnitude is 1.277e-3 (5th percentile 1.92e-3, median 7.47e-3) — only 1.3-1.7x the largest step in a +-1e-3 stencil. So any additive tau design perturbation at that amplitude IS a live hazard for the canonical arm and must be guarded by asserting canonical(corners) is constant over the stencil; the multiplicative Phase-3 stencil is safe. Also confirmed the handover's premise that the context depends only on tau corners here: pos_int/faces come from the node set (identical, ADMITTED_SAME_TRACE) and `known` = [E, nu, gamma, 1/n] is unchanged.

Question 6 (nullspace leak) — see finding 3; the leak cannot reach inv(Mhat).
